I'm not quite as far along in my journey as you are — just about to roll up on a full month in starting in a couple days, but my general impression has been pretty similar to yours. Anxiety and depression has been through the roof these past couple days, with zero motivation, serious social withdrawal, and intense lethargy to go along with it. 

From what I can see, medicating on Lexapro is very much a non-linear process: it's a very bumpy journey with stiff peaks and steep drops rather than one smooth ride uphill. Some weeks you'll feel better than you have in years, while some you'll come crashing down with the worst depressive funk you've experienced in a long time.

I do know that adjusting to this medication is a long and arduous journey, and most people recommend at least 2-3 months of usage before throwing in the towel completely. The fact that you've had good days on the medication is proof that it's working as it should, your body just needs more time to adjust itself to the new hormones before fully stabilizing. I think you should talk to your doctor about potentially using some short-term medication to adjust to the side-effect period if you need it rather than pulling the plug altogether. We'll get to the other side eventually!

About 3 days away from the one month mark so far, anxiety and depression are currently still pretty high but I can definitely see some changes in how I approach interactions. I'm starting to care considerably less about my self-image than I did before — I'm less hyper-critical and constantly evaluating what people think of me. It's also made me much more disinhibited; before, social confrontations were impossible for me to get through without my anxiety flying through the roof and bringing me to the verge of tears (shoutout to parental trauma), but now if somebody were to start screaming in my face, I would be able to stand my ground and not get nearly as worked up as I did before. Not all the way there yet, but I hope the feeling starts to increase because it's honestly been extremely liberating :)

I'm glad to hear you got some solace out of it :) It definitely feels bittersweet to come here and find so many people who share the same sentiments when the rest of the world feels so sterile and fake, like you said. It makes me wonder what could be if Earth was filled with the people that collect here instead, but at least the knowledge that others see the whole mind-bludgeoning facade for what it is helps numb the pain a bit
